title: Scenario Execution Observation
description: Runtime testimony for exactly one canonical execution-vector step (kernel/contracts/execution/scenario-kernel-execution-vector.json) within one scenario execution. Emitted by the kernel body itself — hand-written or projected — as each step completes or fails, via the ExecutionObserver port; never hand-authored by consumer application code. One scenario execution normally produces one observation per canonical step, in canonical order, until the run either completes its final step or stops at the step that failed. See scenario-kernel-execution-closure.schema.json for what a complete trace means, and governance rules K011-K013.

stepId.description: Must match a stepId from the admitted scenario-kernel-execution-vector.v1 instance at kernel/contracts/execution/scenario-kernel-execution-vector.json. Deliberately not a closed enum here: this schema stays valid as the canonical vector evolves under K010, and stepId membership/order is a semantic-authority/conformance concern (see tools/src/conformance/proof/execution-closure-mechanics.ts) rather than something this document validates alone — the same division of labor scenario-kernel-execution-vector.schema.json's own description draws for consumes/produces linkage.

sequence.description: Zero-based position of this step within the canonical execution vector (not within the observed trace) — lets a validator detect a skipped or reordered step without re-deriving canonical order from stepId alone.

status.description: 'observed' is an ordinary completed step. 'admission-rejected' and 'execution-failed' mark the step at which the execution stopped short of completion — a conforming scenario execution has at most one non-'observed' status, and only on its final observation.
